newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Last two former BCCI officials freed from UAE jail.
newsitem.headline: Last two former BCCI officials freed from UAE jail.

text.p: The last two former Bank of Credit and Commerce International officials held in prison in the United Arab Emirates have been released but must remain in the country, judicial sources said Sunday.

They said Hassan Mahmoud Kazmi and Abdul-Hafeez Mohammed Ahmed were released from their Abu Dhabi jail on Wednesday after they completed six-year sentences. The two cannot leave the country pending appeals to the supreme court, the sources said.
BCCI, founded in Luxembourg in 1972, was shut down worldwide by central banks in 1991 when evidence emerged of massive and widespread fraud.

A UAE court last June acquitted two former BCCI officials, but upheld sentences against eight others -- including Kazmi and Ahmed -- saying they must pay $8.3 million in addition to the original in civil damages.
The court also upheld prison sentences imposed on the eight, including Kazmi and Ahmed. The other six have completed their sentences, but were prevented from leaving the UAE pending their appeals.
Most of the defendants are Pakistanis, some of whom also hold British passports.
The Abu Dhabi government, BCCI's biggest shareholder, has agreed to pay $1.5 billion to meet claims by some creditors.
Thirteen former BCCI officials had been tried on charges of fraud, forgery and misappropriation of funds in Abu Dhabi where the disgraced bank had its main offices.

All but one were sentenced in 1994 to jail terms and civil damages of about $9 billion. Of the 12 who were sentenced, 10 have now served their terms but are not allowed to leave the UAE while their appeal proceedings continued. The remaining two were sentenced in absentia.
One has since died. The other is in a U.S. prison for a BCCI-related crime.
